summary: Geshe Kelsang Gyatso was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Chambaling, Tashilhunpo, Ngamring Chöde, and Sera Monastery (~1945–1973) under Trijang Rinpoche. He served as a teacher at Manjushri Kadampa Meditation Centre from 1977.

Geshe Lhakdor works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. He worked at Tibet House New Delhi and became Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 2005.

Geshe Lhundub Sopa specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Gaden Chokor and Sera Monastery under teachers including Geshe Lhundrup Tabkhe. At the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he was Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies (1973), Professor (1985), and Emeritus Professor (1967).
Geshe Lobsang Gyatso worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Drepung Monastery and served as director of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics until 1997.

Geshe Lobsang Jamspal is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 1985–1990), Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and University of Delhi.
Geshe Lobsang Tharchin was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his education at Sera Monastery (Lharampa Geshe, 1953) and Gyume Tantric College.

Geshe Losang Chödar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and served as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics (both attested 2010).

Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments at Leiden University and Drepung Monastery (attested 1966–1995), serving as a Geshe of sGo-mang sgrva-tshang and Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery.

Geshe Palden Drakpa specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as Librarian at Tibet House New Delhi (attested 1987–1992, 2004) and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987.

Geshe Rabten was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1940–1959) under Trijang Rinpoche and later taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, later serving as resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from 1978.

Geshe Tashi Tsering is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera and Gyuto monasteries and under Geshe Thubten Rinchen, later teaching at Kopan Monastery (~1992–1994) and Jamyang Buddhist Centre (from 1994).
Geshe Tsondru Kongpel is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned Geshe degrees at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Wangyal worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Monastery (~1921–1938) and Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Agvan Dorjiev. He taught at Columbia University (~1962–1972) and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (~1958–1983).
Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1991, 2004, and 2014–2019).

Geshe Yeshe Tobden worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lodoe Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche, and taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1971).
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.
Gesshin Myoko Prabhasa Dharma Cheney was a Buddhist studies practitioner who studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki (1967) and Seikaku Hirata.

Gessho Sasaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. At Otani University, he served as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

Gherardo Gnoli was a religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian scholar educated at Sapienza University of Rome. He taught at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008), and served as President of IsMEO (~1979–1995) and IsIAO (~1995–2011).
